text: Manchester encoding guarantees a transition in every bit period. What does it cost?
choices: Half the channel's capacity: it is 50% efficient
explanation: Manchester needs two signal transitions per bit, so it consumes twice the bandwidth for the same data rate — 50% efficiency. That was an acceptable trade for 10BASE-T in 1983 and unthinkable at 10 Gb/s, which is why the efficiency ladder runs to 64B/66B at 96.9%.
